title: Geostatistical Discharge Estimation in Hydroelectric Canals: Integration Kriging, Conditional Simulation, and Sampling Design
content:
Abstract

Accurate discharge estimation in hydroelectric canals is essential for turbine efficiency monitoring and operational decision-making, yet conventional current-meter methods provide no rigorous uncertainty quantification for the integrated discharge quantity. This study proposes a hierarchical geostatistical framework for inference on an integrated hydraulic quantity—namely canal discharge—that treats it as an integrated spatial random field and propagates uncertainty at two complementary levels: (a) integration kriging, which provides optimal discharge estimates and a preliminary uncertainty measure grounded in sampling geometry and variogram structure, enabling sampling-design optimization; and (b) geostatistical conditional simulation, which generates complete probability distributions for discharge conditioned on all observed values, yielding confidence intervals for risk-based decisions. The framework is applied to 36 velocity surveys at the Kootenay Canal (British Columbia, Canada; discharges 38–109 m3 ${\mathrm{m}}^{3}$/s) over two complementary measurement configurations: a sparsely sampled section (∼294 points) and a densely sampled section (∼1,217 points). Three key results emerge. First, integration kriging delivers discharge estimates whose coefficient of variation reaches 0.40% $0.40\%$ in the densely sampled section and 0.74% $0.74\%$ in the sparsely sampled one, comparable to or below the operational repeatability of the current-meter method (± $\pm $0.4%–0.6%). Second, the gap between the kriging-based and simulation-based coefficients of variation narrows as sampling density increases. Third, the framework yields sampling-design curves that quantify the trade-off between measurement density and discharge uncertainty, providing direct operational guidance. These results establish a principled, operationally applicable foundation for uncertainty-aware discharge estimation in hydroelectric canals.
